content:
I do not think the updater interacts with the operating system at that level to cause the effect you are observing. Operating system interactions are few in the Mozilla platform as the actual operating system the code runs on varies a lot. Windows, Mac OS, Linux etc.

You could try disabling the use of a background task in settings to see if that affects any sort of change, but I do not hold out much hope. The silent update is documented here https://wiki.mozilla.org/Windows_Service_Silent_Update

Are you also using Firefox? it has an updater that can update when the application is not open using the windows task scheduler, and that task could prevent windows going to sleep, or even wake the system to do the task I assume, but I don't see it changing the settings.

content:
These are some generic suggestions to avoid problems with anti-virus software.

Create an exception in your anti-virus software for the Thunderbird profile folder, so that the anti-virus real-time scanner will not scan it. https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/profiles-where-thunderbird-stores-user-data#w_how-to-find-your-profile

Don't let your anti-virus software scan incoming and outgoing messages.

Don't let your anti-virus software scan attachments.

Don't let your anti-virus software intercept your secure connection to the server.

Remove any add-ons your anti-virus software may have installed in Thunderbird.

content:
UPDATE: I checked my Message Filter settings and found some possible causes. I had checked "Manually Run", "Periodically", and "Getting New Mail" all at the same time. This seemed to trigger a data-handling conflict under a heavy load.

Looking at my macOS diagnostic logs, the failure unfolded in just 2.25 seconds: - 10:22:33.14: The network hub is acutely overloaded by a sudden flood of IMAP data. - 10:22:33.65: iCloud security hits a timeout because it cannot process the authentication tokens rapidly enough. - 10:22:35.39: Local KeySync triggers a hard lock, permanently freezing the application process.

Making these filter checkbox options mutually exclusive could maybe prevent users from accidentally creating conflicting background loops.

The real, structural solution though is, Mozilla could implement something like decoupling the startup of the visual interface, downloading e-mail, and the background filtering tasks at the same instant.

More testing would need to be done to find the root cause.

[Note: Troubleshooting and formatting done with the assistance of a free AI tool based on my local macOS Console logs and reconstruction of the events.]
